title: Stop a stale dex fetch from repainting the screen
kevin: Art can tap the arrows as fast as he likes and his Pokemon always comes back.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - mashing is how Art plays and it currently strands him with no way back
acceptance: smoke: after 20 synthetic #nav-next clicks 30ms apart and a settle, #types holds at least one .tag, #poke-sprite computed opacity is 1, and #poke-name is neither empty nor 'LOADING'
smoke: after that mash, state.curId equals the id printed in #id-text (a stale response can no longer win and re-seed the arrows)
smoke: a loadPoke() whose fetch rejects after a newer nav has started leaves #types and #stats-area untouched
notes: MECHANISM, verified in source and NOT what the forum diagnosed. There is no reveal animation that restarts and never repaints: pxReveal (fx.js:82-88) and wipeSweep both self-clear on timers longer than their own durations. The real faults are all in loadPoke (dex.js:118-186): (1) there is no in-flight token, and state.curId/state.curData are assigned AFTER the await (dex.js:132-133), so with N taps in flight the screen settles on whichever request resolves last and that stale response also re-seeds the arrows; cache hits resolve instantly while misses take network time, so out-of-order resolution is the NORMAL case when mashing. (2) The catch block (dex.js:140-155) clears #types and #stats-area with no guard at all, so a request abandoned four taps ago can wipe the chips off a Pokemon that already rendered. (3) #poke-sprite.style.opacity=0 is set at dex.js:125 BEFORE the await and only restored inside the guarded branch at 179-185, which also leaves setScanning(true) stuck on when it bails. Take one module-level token at the top of loadPoke and re-check it after EVERY await, including inside the catch. Effort 3 because it is one function but four separate resolution points and the epoch discipline has to be right.

title: The screen wipe must never blank the whole app

acceptance: scenes: a new scene forces #screen-wipe to its mid-sweep keyframe and asserts the top bar and the toolbar are still visible and unobscured (their rects do not intersect the wipe's rect)
notes: #screen-wipe (index.html:20, css/gba.css:70-82) is a position:fixed inset:0 panel at z-index 9400 running wipeSweep 0.45s steps(10,end) in --px-ink, which is dark navy - the exact 'wall of navy' the reviewers describe. It covers the header, the identity strip, the sprite and the whole toolbar at once. Kept separate from B-001 on purpose: this is CSS and markup only, touches no JS, and the two can ship in either order. Do not delete the wipe - it is the app's transition voice - just stop it covering chrome the child needs to escape with.

title: One catch, one save write
kevin: If the tablet ever runs out of room mid-catch, the Pokemon and the ball can't disagree any more.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred
Never take something away from a child
acceptance: smoke: with localStorage.setItem stubbed to throw from the second call onward, a dex catch leaves the save either fully containing the new id (in caught AND in mons) or fully unchanged - never caught-without-mons, and never a spent Master Ball with no catch
smoke: a single dex catch calls persist() exactly once (counted with a spy)
notes: persist() (state.js:240-264) is the only writer and it serialises the WHOLE save each time, so no single write is itself partial - the tearing is a prefix effect across five independent persists in one catch: spendMasterBall (catch.js:49), recordCatch (catch.js:126), ensureMon (catch.js:127), the game-progress listener (catch.js:135 -> progression.js:192/302/344/350) and setNick (catch.js:144). Batch them: defer and flush once. Two things the forum got slightly wrong and the implementer must not repeat: the 'comes back as Lv5' case is caught-without-a-mons-entry falling through to DEFAULT_LEVEL (state.js:310,328), and the genuinely destructive case is the ball being spent before the catch lands. persist() returns false on failure and NO caller checks it - the flush must check and roll the in-memory save back. Do NOT change the save shape.

title: Cap the species cache so it can't fill the tablet
kevin: Browsing the whole Pokedex can no longer eat the room the boys' collections live in.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - the cache and the save share one 5MB box
acceptance: smoke: after seeding 400 synthetic pkmn: entries, pokedexos_apicache_v2 holds at most the cap (oldest evicted first) and its serialised length stays under 1.5MB
smoke: a cache eviction never removes or damages pokedexos_save_v2
notes: CACHE_KEY is pokedexos_apicache_v2 (api.js:10); the single writer is saveCache (api.js:14-23). There is no cap, no LRU, no TTL. The only eviction is reactive inside the quota catch (api.js:17-21): drop move: keys, retry once, then set cache={} in memory WITHOUT removeItem, so a stale on-disk blob outlives an empty in-memory view. Count entries honestly: getPokemon deliberately stores each species twice, under a name key and an id key (api.js:142-143). Most of the ~8-9KB per species is slimPokemon keeping the entire moves array (api.js:61) - trimming that is a cheaper alternative but battle move selection reads it, so price that before choosing. The file header comment ('~2-3KB each, 151 Pokemon = 450KB') is stale in two ways and should be corrected while you are in there: MAX_POKEMON is 649.

title: A grown-up can always get back into Parent Tools
kevin: If one of the boys sets the PIN, you are not locked out of your own save.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - the only in-app route back to a lost save can be claimed by a child
acceptance: smoke: with a PIN stored, the pad offers a recovery route that clears pokedexos_devpin while leaving pokedexos_save_v2 byte-identical
smoke: the recovery route cannot be completed by tapping alone - a wrong attempt leaves the gate shut and the existing 'wrong PIN keeps the pad up' check still passes
notes: requirePin (devtools.js:223-233) is trust-on-first-use: if no PIN is stored it just sets one, with no proof of who is asking. There is no removeItem of PIN_KEY anywhere in the repo, the PIN is per-device localStorage and is not in the save, and it gates PASTE CODE, LOAD FILE, UNDO IMPORT and Parent Tools - i.e. the entire restore path. The only documented way back is a devtools console command on a device with no F12. Whatever you build must not become a bypass a 7-year-old can walk: prefer something that needs an artefact the child does not have (the exported save code or file) or a long hold plus a word printed in the README. Fail closed on every branch, the way requirePin already does.

title: Silence should look like silence
kevin: The button that turns the sound off stops looking like a NO sign, and it keeps its shape.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - one unlabelled tap removes Art's whole non-verbal channel
acceptance: smoke: toggling #music-btn twice leaves its .btn-glyph child element intact (assert the span still exists after each toggle)
smoke: the muted glyph string differs from #cry-btn's glyph string
notes: A real bug nobody filed sits underneath the design complaint: syncMusicBtn (settings.js:19-22) assigns btn.innerText, which DESTROYS the <span class='btn-glyph'> the markup provides (index.html:40) and replaces it with a bare text node. After the first toggle the glyph permanently loses its sizing and alignment and never gets it back. Use querySelector('.btn-glyph').textContent. Then the design half: with sound off the child sees a red prohibition circle, which to a four-year-old reads 'you are not allowed', and with sound on it is the SAME speaker glyph as the CRY button in his own toolbar. Make the off state a picture of silence (a full-size speaker with one slash, or a note fading) and give CRY a different glyph. Leave the storage alone: pokedexos_muted is deliberately device-wide, not per-player (audio.js:62, 85-90), and that is a defensible choice - the editor upheld only the legibility risk, not the sharing.

title: Say which round you are standing in
kevin: Gabe can tell at a glance whether he is looking at the circuit he has beaten or the one he hasn't started.

notes: READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYTHING - THE FORUM'S DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND THE FIX IT ASKS FOR WOULD BREAK WORKING CODE. Round 2 is NOT displaying Round 1's data. beatenCount, gymUnlocked, trainerUnlocked, totalBeaten and recordGymWin are all round-parameterised (gym.js:57-72, 250), trainerKey appends ':r2' (gymdata.js:178), renderGymList re-derives the round on every read (gym.js:104), and smoke already asserts 'round 2 raises every trainer by 15 and keeps round 1 untouched'. What E-0067 actually shows is the ROUND 1 board, correctly reading 58/58, with the title 'GYM CIRCUIT' - while the UNSELECTED ROUND 2 tab is painted gold and the SELECTED Round 1 tab is var(--paper) against var(--paper-2), a difference of almost nothing (gba.css:1849-1853). Two experienced reviewers concluded from it that the entire endgame was finished. That is the bug: gold means 'the hard good thing' AND 'selected' at the same time, and the lure wins. Give the selected tab a mark that is not a fill. T-006 and eight sibling machine threads are the missing space in the same tab's label ('CROWN-emoji' immediately followed by 'ROUND 2', gym.js:115) - fix it here while the file is open. Do NOT rewrite the round data model.

title: The endgame's numbers stop being the faintest thing on screen

title: The battle's words wait for its pictures
kevin: Pressing an attack lets you watch it land before the other Pokemon takes its turn.
acceptance: smoke: with PACE.fast=false, the log line for the second attacker is not written until the first attacker's .bar-ghost transition has completed (assert on a recorded timeline of logMsg timestamps against transitionend)
notes: RISKIER THAN ITS SEVERITY SUGGESTS - see the report. performAttack (battle.js:974-1028) fires updateHP and impactFx at 1006-1008 and then returns after awaitOrTap(300) at 1027, while .bar-ghost is a 300ms delay plus a 600ms transition (main.css:223) - so the enemy's line prints roughly 600ms before the bar it describes has finished draining, and the strongest feedback a child gets for pressing a button is watching his own Pokemon take damage. FOUR THINGS THAT WILL BITE: (1) awaitOrTap resolves early on tap once PACE.floor elapses, so any plain delay you add is skippable and a mashing child re-opens the gap - use the {beat:true} form (config.js:139) or the hitStop precedent in fx.js:74-80. (2) PACE.fast clamps everything to 250ms for the suite, so the test must drive it with fast off. (3) performAttack is shared by wild, gym, versus (battle.js:1942) and the switch-punish path (922) - three modes change at once. (4) Every await must stay behind the stale(e) epoch checks at 975, 982, 997 and 1005 or you resurrect the teardown race, which is the single most common source of real bugs in this file. Effort 3 and it cannot be split: the fix is one ordering rule in one function.

title: Endurance HP where the fight is

smoke: after the heal, every slot in that strip reads full

And the heal feedback is not merely faint - it is ABSENT from this screen: pokeCenterHeal writes #gym-center-msg (gym.js:45-49), an element emitted only by renderGymList on the HUB (gym.js:156), so from inside a stop the `if (el)` guard silently no-ops. title: A shiny should look shiny everywhere
kevin: Gabe's rare black Charizard is actually black in his box and on his Pokedex page.
acceptance: smoke: with id 4 in player.shinies, the PC tile img src and the dex #poke-sprite src both resolve to the shiny sprite path without pressing SHINY
notes: Nothing is missing from the data: slimPokemon already caches front_shiny, back_shiny, official_shiny and both animated shinies (api.js:48-59). Two gaps. And the dex's SHINY chip is a manual toggle on state.isShiny (dex.js:293-325) that never consults player().shinies. Only battle.js honours shiny sprites, and only for freshly rolled wild ones. A shiny is the rarest thing a seven-year-old can own and the whole point is that it LOOKS different; right now every sparkle in his box is a promise the picture does not keep.

title: Deep Forest keeps its promise
kevin: The card that says what lives in a place tells the truth about it.
acceptance: smoke: no habitat sub-label contains a word that is not a real Pokemon type (catches 'BIRD') and none mixes a rarity word into the type row (catches 'ULTRA RARE')
smoke: for every habitat, at least 80% of its common pool matches one of its advertised types

The 'species with no home get dumped in the forest' theory is FALSE - habitatfill.js is a generated explicit id table per habitat with no catch-all bucket; forest is simply the largest, having absorbed the bug/grass/flying overflow. Related coverage note worth knowing before you edit the table: smoke's 'all 649 species reachable in the world' check counts habitat pools PLUS gym rosters, so a handful of species are reachable only as trainer spoils and can never be met in EXPLORE. That is not what this item fixes, but do not be surprised by it.

title: Grown-up Pokemon in grown-up places
kevin: Once Gabe is strong, the wild starts showing him evolved Pokemon instead of babies with big numbers.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - the low-level species must stay catchable
acceptance: smoke: over 200 rolls in a habitat whose level band is 40 or higher, no rolled species is one that evolves below that level
notes: rollEncounter (explore.js:276-284) picks a rarity tier and then a raw id from static c/u/r/L arrays; the level is computed completely separately (battle.js:304-306) and never feeds back into the species choice. So a champion meets a Lv57 Koffing - a thing that cannot exist in the wild anywhere else in Pokemon - and his dex will never once show him an evolved form appearing in the grass. Effort 3 and it is not splittable: EXPLORE must not depend on the network, so this needs a local evolution-stage table. habitatfill.js is the precedent - it is generated into the repo by a tool - so follow that pattern rather than fetching chains at runtime. Do NOT remove the base forms from the pools; swap the weighting as the band climbs, so nothing a child could previously catch becomes uncatchable.

title: The rematch button leads with the prize
kevin: The green buttons Gabe sees most say what he wins instead of what he loses.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - the only label on a returning player's button is a halved reward
acceptance: smoke: a beaten trainer's CTA contains 'CATCH THEIR TEAM' and does not lead with 'HALF XP'; the existing smoke check that a beaten trainer offers a REMATCH still passes
notes: The label is one string at gym.js:206 and 'HALF XP' is the most repeated text on the page - five times down one screen, on the button a returning player presses most. IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: the economics half of the merged group (F-067's 'the endgame is Lv8 Geodudes at half rate') is ALREADY FIXED and shipped in v19.8.0 - roundTrainers applies +15 levels (gymdata.js:145-163) and a first Round-2 win pays FULL xp because the rematch flag reads the round's own key (battle.js:373, 1256). title: Tell the four balls apart
kevin: Gabe can see which ball is better before he spends it.
rule_risk: Junior Mode must never advertise its accommodations
acceptance: smoke: the four rows of #ballpick-list carry four DIFFERENT captions

The app already solves it two taps away: the dex drawer ranks them 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 100% (index.html:99-104). Carry that across. WHERE I DISAGREE WITH F-035: it proposes giving Art one/two/three pips so the ladder is a shape. Do not. Art's balls always succeed, so a ladder would be a lie, and F-119 praises this drawer specifically for keeping the secret - junior already hides .ball-count (gba.css:637). title: Super effective should be a colour, not a triangle
kevin: The move that will really hurt looks different from the move that won't.
acceptance: smoke: the .tile-eff badge's computed colour differs between a super-effective tile and a not-very-effective tile
smoke: a 4x hit renders a distinct data-eff state from a 2x hit
notes: EFF_GLYPH (battle.js:531) supplies up/down arrows and .tile-eff (gba.css:1055) sets position and size but NO colour, so both states inherit the tile's own ink and the one tactical decision the fight asks a child to make is encoded in the direction of a six-pixel triangle. Colour is free here and this game uses colour brilliantly everywhere else. Second half: effOf (battle.js:533-540) collapses every multiplier above 1 into 'super', discarding the 4 that getTypeMultiplier genuinely returns (config.js:73-85) - so a 4x hit wears the badge a plain 2x gets. Touch effOf, EFF_GLYPH, moveTilesHtml, refreshMoveEff and the [data-eff] rules together. Keep the badge on in junior; that is deliberate (battle.js:527-529). Note the tile RING already differs (gold for super, dark for weak, gba.css:1075-1085) and the in-arena impact marks are already colour-coded - the badge is the only monochrome part of the chain.

title: Two moves of one type must not look identical
kevin: Art's four attack buttons are four different buttons.
acceptance: smoke: for a Pokemon with two same-type, same-power moves, the two rendered tiles differ in at least two of {icon, power dots, dup stripe} and are not pixel-identical
notes: PARTLY FALSE AS FILED - two differentiators already exist and the implementer should not re-invent them: power dots computed as ceil(power/40) (battle.js:559, 571) and a data-dup='1' diagonal stripe on the second and later tiles of a repeated type (battle.js:560, gba.css:1068-1070). What remains true is the narrow case the colourist actually photographed: two Normal moves of EQUAL power come down to the stripe alone, and at 20px on a phone that stripe is not enough for a four-year-old. Cheapest honest fix is to make the dup stripe much louder in junior, or add per-move icons for the small set of commonly duplicated moves. One trap documented in the code: the tile uses background-color, never the background shorthand, because the shorthand wipes the stripe (battle.js:563-564).

title: Give the PC box its type colours
kevin: Green Pokemon stop vanishing into the green box, and both boys can find things by colour.
acceptance: smoke: every .pc-item carries a data-type attribute and its card face is derived from typeColors, so no two type groups share the same background
notes: itemHtml (pc.js:238-253) and stickerHtml (258-266) emit no type information at all, so all 649 cards are the same rgba(107,255,107,0.06) on the same dark green CRT (gba.css:416-418) and roughly a fifth of the collection - every Grass and most Bug - is camouflaged. Sampled: Caterpie against its own card is 2.38:1, Metapod is a pale green blob. Charmander reads fine at a near-identical luminance because orange against green is a hue apart, which is the tell: it is the card, not the sprites. This one change also delivers F-040's wish for free - the type palette already exists and is already good, it is just used in exactly one place - giving Art a box he can sort by colour with a finger and Gabe a 649-slot grid he can scan by hue. The junior sticker face (gba.css:1541) has the same flatness in cream; do both.

title: Tapping a Pokemon keeps you in the box
kevin: Tapping one of his 620 no longer throws Gabe back to the Pokedex and loses his place.
acceptance: smoke: tapping a PC tile in normal mode leaves #pc-modal visible and opens a card showing that Pokemon's own level, nickname and shiny state
smoke: closing that card restores the grid's previous scrollTop
notes: handlePCSelect (pc.js:328-344) hard-closes the modal and calls loadPoke(id), which renders the GENERIC species record - nothing on that path reads player().shinies, monLevel or nickOf, so the shiny, the level and the nickname the tile itself was showing are all dropped. He asked about HIS Charmander and got the encyclopedia article. Scroll position dies because reopening runs renderGrid, which replaces #pc-grid.innerHTML wholesale (pc.js:94); currentGen survives, scrollTop does not, and in a 620 box that scroll was the expensive part. Junior already does the right thing here - openSticker (pc.js:412-443) opens a card in place with the box still behind it - so this is 'make normal behave like junior', not new UI. The editor asked for this to be fixed alongside B-036, which is the opposite failure on the same control.

title: An uncaught shadow should still answer a poke
kevin: When Art prods a Pokemon he hasn't caught yet, something happens.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes - a dead-feeling tap teaches a four-year-old the pictures are not for touching
acceptance: scenes: tapping an uncaught .pc-item in junior mode changes at least one measured box or paint property that the baseline records, and the change is still visible 300ms after the tap
notes: THE JUNIOR HALF OF F-013 IS FALSE and the correction changes the fix entirely. Junior taps DO open a card: handlePCSelect routes straight to openSticker (pc.js:331). What the reviewer hit was an UNCAUGHT sticker, which deliberately answers with a 320ms .tease shake and no modal (pc.js:413-418) - and in the junior book every one of the 649 slots is rendered (pc.js:294), so on a fresh save every tile on screen is a grey shadow that wiggles briefly and does nothing else. The two 'byte-identical' screenshots the editor verified with md5 are consistent with the shake having simply finished before the harness fired. So the real defect is that the answer is too small and too brief to survive a four-year-old's attention, not that there is no answer. Give it something that lands and stays for a beat - a silhouette lift, a soft thud - so 'not yet' reads as an answer rather than a broken button. This is the thread F-002 is really about: a pre-reader's whole vocabulary for 'tell me about this' is poking the picture.

title: Fill the six holes at the top of Art's box
kevin: The six empty boxes on Art's favourite screen finally mean something.
acceptance: scenes: in the sticker-book scene with zero favourites, every .fav-slot contains a child element (a ghost star, or a recent-catch sprite) - none is an empty div
notes:
renderFavShelf (pc.js:375-389) emits literally '
' six times, unconditionally, with no :empty guard in the CSS (gba.css:1591-1597) - so the first thing a pre-reader sees on his favourite screen is six empty dashed rectangles that never fill and never explain themselves. The code comment at pc.js:374 calls them 'an invitation'; there is no glyph, no ghost, nothing to invite with. Three reviewers found this independently and all three landed on the same fix. F-030's version is the best one and costs nothing: until he has starred anything, fill the shelf with his last six catches as sprites - it turns the emptiest thing on the screen into the warmest, welcomes a boy back after three weeks without mentioning that he was gone, and only ever adds. The editor explicitly did NOT uphold the 'this punishes Art' framing - an empty shelf is not a punishment - so do not treat this as a rule-2 fix; treat it as the first thing he looks at meaning something.

title: Art sees more than nine at a time
kevin: More of Art's collection fits on screen and less of it is header.
acceptance: scenes: in the sticker-book scene at 375x667 the .pc-grid occupies at least 55% of the viewport height
notes: Measured chrome today is about 359px of 667 - 54% - before a single sticker appears: 40px modal padding, 49px header, 64px favourites shelf, 66px team strip, 70px tab row, 73px close button. Shorten the header, or collapse the favourites shelf while it is empty - B-037 may deliver that for free, so sequence them. DO NOT shrink the sticker tiles: scenes.mjs already asserts an 88px sticker floor and F-104's explore-card geometry is the template the whole junior mode is measured against. B-039 is the other half of the answer.

title: A picture lens for the ones he's proudest of
kevin: One tap fills the box with just the sparkly ones, or just the newest.
acceptance: smoke: the PC exposes NEWEST, SHINY and FAVES chips that re-filter the grid without hiding the generation tabs, and each chip renders as an icon with no required text
notes: Gabe's twelve shinies are the twelve he is proudest of and the only way to reach them is scrolling 620 cards looking for a sparkle - which happens to work today only because they sit at #001-#012; the next shiny at #430 ends that. Same for the newest catch, which files itself into dex order and vanishes at row 143, so the moment of pride has nowhere to go. Icons only, so the same control works identically in Art's book - he cannot read G1 either, and a sparkle chip that fills his screen with just the special ones is the single best thing to hand a four-year-old with 620 Pokemon. It is a LENS, not a filter that hides: nothing is removed and the gen tabs stay.

title: SAVE FILE says what it did
kevin: The backup button tells you the filename instead of looking like nothing happened.
acceptance: smoke: tapping #set-export-file opens a dialog naming the file, and a stubbed failure opens a dialog that says it failed
notes: downloadSaveFile (settings.js:87-100) ends at URL.revokeObjectURL with no dialog, no status line, no sound and no haptic - while COPY CODE in the very same row (settings.js:75-85) confirms properly with a floppy-disk card. This is the one button Kevin presses on a Sunday morning before touching anything, and on an installed iOS PWA a programmatic a.click() download is exactly the case that silently does nothing - in which case this screen looks identical to the screen that worked. Two extras worth doing while you are here: revokeObjectURL fires on the very next line after click(), which can race the download in some engines; and navigator.share({files}) is supported on the boys' iPad per CLAUDE.md and appears nowhere in the repo - it is the better primitive for getting a save off a tablet. As Kevin put it, he would rather it lied loudly than succeeded in silence.

title: The version number you can actually read
kevin: After a push you can tell at a glance whether the iPad got the new version.
acceptance: scenes: #boot-version measures at least 4.5:1 against the boot screen background
scenes: the Settings VERSION row is not inside the card-section labelled SOUND
notes: Measured 1.58:1 and the reviewer's arithmetic checks out: .boot-version is var(--paper-2) at opacity .75 (gba.css:1812-1815) composited over #8bac0f (main.css:11), landing at about rgb(203,205,136) on rgb(139,172,15), at 8px. At arm's length on a kitchen table 19.8.0 and 18.8.0 are indistinguishable. The Settings instance is fine on contrast but is filed between MUSIC & SOUND and BUZZ under a heading that says SOUND (index.html:400-403) - the version of the game is not a sound setting. This is the only diagnostic a non-developer has, and a stale cached shell looks exactly like a working one.

title: Yesterday's collection, kept
kevin: The game quietly keeps a spare copy every day, and tells you when you last saved one yourself.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred
acceptance: smoke: on the first boot of a new local day a dated backup key appears holding the previous save verbatim, and at most N are retained
smoke: Settings shows a LAST BACKED UP line that reads NEVER on a fresh device and a date after an export
notes: The game already knows how to hold a second save shape - it does it on every import - but only when a grown-up is standing at the Settings screen. Every other day of the year there is exactly one copy of both boys' collections, in one browser key, on one tablet. Today's only routine second copy is pokedexos_save_v2_prev (state.js:8), written ONLY by importCode (state.js:475): nothing snapshots before removeMon (devtools.js:110) or before a normal session, and restorePreviousSave writes the displaced save back into the same slot (state.js:305), so a second UNDO walks you forward again rather than two deep. There IS a dated key already - pokedexos_save_corrupt_<timestamp> (state.js:9,198) - but it is written only on an unreadable save, is never read back anywhere, and its own setItem is inside a try that gives up silently when storage is full. 21KB per copy. NO SAVE-SHAPE CHANGE: these are sibling keys. Sequence after B-004 - the backups live in the same 5MB box the cache is currently eating.

title: Ask before you hand over the other brother's game
kevin: One stray tap can't drop Art into Gabe's champion save any more.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - one accidental tap gives edit rights over the other brother's collection
acceptance: smoke: tapping #player-btn opens a confirm showing both players' lead sprites, and state.currentPlayer does not change until it is accepted
smoke: cancelling the confirm leaves any in-progress gym run intact
notes: togglePlayer (main.js:111-115) switches players on one tap of a chip about a centimetre wide sitting right beside the Pokeball everybody taps first, with no confirm and no undo - and it lands you in the other boy's PC box with full edit rights over his collection. The only guard is 'not mid-catch, not mid-battle'. There is a second, quieter cost the forum missed: setPlayer also calls clearGymRun (main.js:107), so a stray tap silently discards a half-finished gym run and its endurance HP. #whoplaying-modal already draws exactly the two-face card this needs (main.js:127-133) - the screen F-019 praises - so reuse it rather than inventing a dialog.

title: Ticks that go somewhere permanent
kevin: Yesterday's finished quests are counted forever instead of vanishing at midnight.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - yesterday's four completed quests are deleted overnight
acceptance: smoke: completing a quest increments player.stats.questsDone; the value survives a reload and a day rollover; a save written before this change still loads with the field defaulted
notes: SCHEMA TOUCH, BUT THE SAFE KIND - follow the existing precedent exactly. stats is {catches, battlesWon, battlesLost, versusWins} (state.js:73), merged shallowly at state.js:146, and `explores` is already an undeclared latecomer written by explore.js:299 and read defensively as (p.stats.explores || 0) at progression.js:388. Do the same: additive, always defaulted on read, no version bump, no migration. p.quests is wiped whenever the day changes (progression.js:190) and allDone is per-day, so there is no aggregate anywhere today. This is not a streak and must not become one - it only ever counts up.

title: SPARKLE stops being a slot machine
kevin: The last badge on the card is something the boys can work towards, like all the others.
acceptance: smoke: after N catches with no shiny the next encounter's shiny roll is guaranteed and the counter resets on a shiny
smoke: the SPARKLE badge's progress fraction moves as that counter climbs
notes: battle.js:302-303 is a stateless roll - 1/50, or 1/10 on the day's sparkle spot - with no counter and no floor. Every other locked badge on that card names a price the boys can pay and shows their exact distance, which is the thing F-069 praises as the best-designed part of the economy; this one cannot be made to move, and the dex has a SHINY button that shows Gabe exactly what he is not getting. It is a dice roll wearing a progress counter, aimed at a seven-year-old. Two acceptable answers and Kevin should pick: a pity floor (additive stats field, same precedent as B-044) or dropping the 0/1 so it is a surprise rather than a scoreboard. Do not lower the odds for Art or say anything about them - his roll is already the same as Gabe's and that is correct.

title: Keep the pixel font inside the app
kevin: In the car with no signal the game still looks like itself.
acceptance: smoke: the offline shell list contains the local font file, and index.html issues no request to fonts.googleapis.com
notes: Press Start 2P is the whole voice of this app and it is the one asset that is not in the app: a remote stylesheet at index.html:11-13, absent from SHELL_FILES (sw.js:19-28), reachable only through the runtime asset branch and therefore cached only AFTER a first successful online load. So the first no-signal launch renders the entire game in Courier - legible, but a different app, and the one the boys would meet in the car. It also breaks every 8px pixel-metric the layout assumes. The woff2 is about 10KB. ASK KEVIN FIRST: committing a binary asset is the closest thing in this backlog to a build step. It is a file, not a pipeline, but CLAUDE.md says ask. Bonus: it also fixes any guest wifi that blocks Google Fonts, and it removes the reason the review corpus cannot see accented capitals (see B-051).

title: A bad second of wifi must not break a sprite
kevin: A Pokemon they caught can't lose its picture permanently.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - a caught Pokemon can permanently lose its picture
acceptance: smoke: a sprite request that fails is not written into pokedexos-assets, asserted against the caching predicate directly
smoke: an entry already stored from a failed response is re-fetched rather than served
notes: sw.js:98 accepts `resp.ok || resp.type === 'opaque'`, and an opaque response is status 0 whether it was a picture or a 404 or a rate-limit - the browser will not say which. The shell branch is strict by comparison (sw.js:79). Then nothing ever repairs it: ASSET_CACHE is the version-independent 'pokedexos-assets' (sw.js:17) and activate only deletes keys ending in '-shell' (sw.js:50), so a release bump will not clear it and nothing prunes it. One flaky minute on hotel wifi and whichever Pokemon the boys were looking at is a blank ball until someone clears site data - which is also where the saves live. Options: request sprites with an explicit cors mode so ok means something, or sanity-check the stored response's size/type. This only bites now that the worker actually installs (v19.8.1), which is why it was invisible before.

title: Fetch the next Pokemon before he asks
kevin: Pressing NEXT paints straight away instead of leaving an empty stage.
acceptance: smoke: after an entry settles, getPokemon has been called for the neighbouring ids within one second, and a NEXT tap onto a warmed neighbour renders with zero new network calls
notes: SEQUENCE THIS AFTER B-001. Prefetching on top of the current unguarded race would make out-of-order resolution MORE likely, not less - the token has to land first. There is no prefetch anywhere today: nav (dex.js:332-339) mutates state.curId and calls loadPoke, and loadPoke awaits getPokemon then getSpecies then the evolution chain serially, each with an 8s timeout. On a throttled phone profile the reviewer measured 700-1450ms per NEXT. This costs no extra data on average - those bytes were going to be fetched one tap later; it just moves the fetch into the seconds the child is already standing still. The reviewer's other suggestion is worth taking: show the already-downloaded still PNG in the spotlight until the 30KB animated one arrives.

title: Don't download cries nobody can hear
kevin: The game stops spending data on sounds that are switched off.
acceptance: smoke: with pokedexos_muted=1, rendering a dex entry issues zero requests to the cries host
notes: setCry (audio.js:280-285) constructs new Audio(url) on every dex render (dex.js:255), and new Audio defaults to preload=auto, so the .ogg downloads before anyone presses CRY. Mute is consulted only at playback time (audio.js:328-330), never here. SCOPE CORRECTION that halves this thread's importance: canPlayOgg() (audio.js:266-273) already means Safari constructs no Audio object and issues no request at all - so this wastes bandwidth on Chrome and Android only, not on the boys' iPad, and the '237KB on their phones' figure in the thread is wrong. Still worth the one-line guard. Nothing about the chiptune fallback (synthCry, audio.js:300) changes.

title: Take me to one I haven't got
kevin: Gabe can jump to the next Pokemon he is missing instead of guessing numbers.
acceptance: smoke: the new control lands on the lowest uncaught id above the current one and wraps at MAX_POKEMON
smoke: on a fully-caught save it does not move and does not error, and plain NEXT still steps by exactly one
notes: nav (dex.js:332-339) is pure plus-or-minus-one with wraparound, and randomPoke (327-330) is uniform over all 649 and ignores caught entirely. Ownership shows up on the dex only as the CATCH button turning into OWNED (dex.js:104-116) - there is no dimming, no gap-scanning, nothing. Gabe has 447 missing and Kanto is 100% done, so pressing NEXT anywhere in the first 151 is a guaranteed dud and his only tool is typing numbers into the search box. Rule 3: ADD the control, never replace plain NEXT with it. The uncaught-dimming grammar he is asking for already exists in the PC box (gba.css:1554-1557) and could be borrowed.

title: The E that isn't in the font
kevin: POKEDEX stops having a small stray letter in the middle of it.
acceptance: smoke: no element rendered in the pixel font has textContent matching an uppercase accented Latin capital
notes: Press Start 2P has no accented capitals, so every uppercase E-acute drops to a fallback typeface and comes back as a small lowercase letter wedged inside the capitals - in the loudest label on three of the most-visited screens. Eight live strings: index.html:99 POKEBALL, :246 SWITCH POKEMON, :435 ADD A POKEMON, :480 POKEDEX, pc.js:349, gym.js:154 POKE CENTER, battle.js:1552, explore.js:325. The boot logo is set in Courier and is fine, as is any genuine lowercase e-acute. WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT: the harness stubs the Google Fonts request with an empty stylesheet, so every screenshot in the review corpus renders in Courier - which HAS the accented capital. The same blind spot means the corpus under-reports clipping everywhere, because the real pixel font is about 40% wider. Worth pairing with B-046, which removes the stub's reason to exist.

title: The ALL tab should look like a group of Pokemon
kevin: The last tab in Art's sticker book stops being a book inside the book.
acceptance: scenes: in the sticker-book scene the final tab contains no book glyph and is sprite-based like the other five

Worse, the identical glyph is the STICKERS button he pressed to GET here (index.html:95), so the picture that means 'go to the book' is now sitting inside the book, and on a full save pressing it produces a grid that looks much like the one already on screen: a dead tap, and dead taps are how a four-year-old decides a control is broken. The two are independent literals, not a shared constant. Fix stays wordless: the five starters shrunk and overlapped, or a rainbow of the five tab colours.

title: Pin down Art's sticker book before someone tidies it
kevin: The screen Art understands best can't be accidentally redesigned away.
acceptance: scenes: uncaught tiles render as pure silhouettes, not greyscaled sprites

scenes: the generation tabs are sprite images, not text labels
scenes: the lead team slot is marked by colour and position with no LEAD word, and all six slots fit on one row at 375
scenes: Art's ball drawer shows no rate, no count and no caption

This is the only screen that briefs Art: colour means mine, shadow means not mine yet, big green arrow means out - and he worked all three out unaided. The last assertion is the important one and it is a RULE-2 TRIPWIRE rather than a layout check: the instinct to be helpful and add a caption or a count to Art's drawer will come back, and the day it does, the accommodation starts advertising itself. junior already hides .ball-count (gba.css:637); assert it stays hidden. Also worth carrying F-084's one caveat into a follow-up: Art's gold lead tint is tan-on-cream and much quieter than Gabe's gold border.

title: Pin down the battle's wordless channel
kevin: The one screen Art can play without help stays that way.
acceptance: smoke: during turn resolution exactly one move tile is at full opacity with a highlight ring and every other battle control is dimmed and inert

smoke: for a caught species the dex shows the ball glyph AND a green tick action bar; for an uncaught one, neither

Compare the dex, which has no lockout at all and goes blank under the same fingers (B-001). F-059's redundancy rule is the other one worth nailing: caught-ness is told twice, by shape AND by colour, so a pre-reader who confuses red and green still has ball-versus-tick. If a refactor ever ships an OWNED state that differs only by its text, this is the check that catches it.

title: Pin down the generous parts of the economy
kevin: The things that make coming back worth it can't quietly disappear.

F-099's degradation philosophy is the other: a hand-drawn inline-SVG Pokeball rather than the web's grey broken-image icon, which would read to Art as 'you broke it'. If a future change adds a YOU ARE OFFLINE modal, this should go red. Note B-018 fixes the one path where that fallback currently fails.

title: Give the first minute one obvious thing to press
kevin: A brand-new save points at the first thing to do, and shows the count ticking from 0 to 1.

On a fresh save the dex is ten equally pressable buttons, nothing says the boy has caught zero, and 0/649 exists exactly once in the whole game - two taps deep behind CARD, on the card Art cannot read. Put the same glow on CATCH while caught is 0, and put a small permanent ball-and-number on the dex. First press, first GOTCHA, first digit ticks. Costs nobody anything.

title: A badge for finishing a region
kevin: Finishing all 151 of Kanto is finally something the game notices.
acceptance: smoke: catching every id in a generation awards that generation's badge exactly once, it renders with a live fraction like every other locked badge, and existing badge ids are unchanged

BADGES ARE DATA-DRIVEN and this is genuinely additive: BADGES is a plain exported array (progression.js:45-68) of {id, emoji, name, desc, check, progress}, the card renders them generically via badgeTile, and checkBadges auto-pays a Master Ball per new badge. Two cautions: badge ids are persisted in p.badges and hydrated unvalidated (state.js:164), so ids must never be reused or renamed; and there is no region concept anywhere in js/ today, so this needs its own id-range table.

title: Tell me what today's quest pays
kevin: Each quest shows its prize as a picture, so Gabe can choose which one to do first.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - a daily reward must not create a streak
acceptance: smoke: every rendered .card-quest row contains a prize element (sprite or icon plus a number) and no quest row shows a streak or a consecutive-day count

The quests are asking for work and naming no wage. A picture on the row is enough. THE CAUTION IS PART OF THE ITEM, not a footnote: these reset daily, so show the prize and never show a streak he can break. That is why the acceptance line asserts the absence as well as the presence.

title: Let Gabe give Art a Pokemon
kevin: The big brother can hand the little one something, with a ribbon on it.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - this writes into a second player's save

Follow the favourites precedent: additive, defaulted, dropped on load if it refers to something unowned (there are already smoke checks shaped exactly like that). The reason to want it is not the Pokemon: right now the only thing a 620-strong collection lets the older brother do is be further ahead, and this gives him something to do with it that makes the little one happier.

A third card on WHO'S PLAYING, a pokeball with no name, a scratch save thrown away when they go home. Effort 3 and schema-touching: a third player slot has to be additive and invisible to older code, and the hydrate path validates players 1 and 2 by name (state.js:148). Ask Kevin before starting - this is the largest save-shape question in the backlog.

title: A gauntlet: five trainers, one health bar
kevin: Once a gym is beaten, there is a harder way to do it again that uses what is already there.

Clear it and a ribbon lights next to that stop's badge. It is real difficulty without inventing a trainer or raising a level, and it makes a Lv8-13 roster mean something again to a Lv62 team. Rules-safe by construction: he opts in, and if he falls over at trainer four nothing is taken - he keeps the badge, keeps the Pokemon, and the ribbon is simply not lit yet. title: Pack their Pokemon for the car
kevin: Before a journey the game quietly saves the pictures they actually own.
acceptance: smoke: on a warm start the worker is asked to cache the team's sprites and the four ball icons, and the request is throttled so it never runs more than N at a time
notes: Now that the worker installs (v19.8.1) the shell is safe but the pictures still are not: sprites only cache after they have been looked at, and even the four balls in the drawer are remote PNGs - so a boy scrolling to a Pokemon he has never opened gets a blank ball, and if the drawer was never opened on wifi it is four blank balls. Warm the certain things - the six on the team, the four ball icons, then everything already caught, oldest first, a few at a time so it never competes with the game. Nothing new appears on screen. SEQUENCE AFTER B-047: warming the cache while it still accepts opaque failures would poison it faster. The reviewer's second idea is worth its own line someday - a small pokeball on the boot screen, filled when the app is fully packed - because it would have shown Kevin in one glance that the worker had never installed.

title: A wind-down that never takes anything away
kevin: At the end of the evening the game gets sleepy instead of shutting a door.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - a wind-down must refuse nothing
acceptance: smoke: with a wind-down length set, nothing becomes disabled or unavailable, no timer value is written into the save, and the trainer card still records no minutes of clock
notes: Thirty-three screens of a simulated Saturday and not one of them is a resting place: the victory modal's only button is CONTINUE, the dex's two biggest buttons are EXPLORE and GYMS, and the end of a session is a wall of green REMATCH bars. Every exit is a door further in. Build this as the OPPOSITE of a lockout: after a length Kevin sets, green fades to dusk, EXPLORE and GYMS go quiet, and the PC box opens by itself on today's catches with their cries - a goodnight card made of the sprites he earned rather than a sentence. The acceptance line encodes the rule that matters: the app currently keeps no clock on the children anywhere, and the clock belongs in Kevin's hands, not in the save.

title: Let a shiny stop the clock
kevin: When something rare turns up, the game waits so Art can enjoy it.

What is still true is the moment of ARRIVAL: a shiny Pidgey turns up, the whole celebration is a line of text Art cannot read, and the next thing that happens is the Pidgey attacks him. Freeze the turn loop, pulse the sprite, play its cry (B-011 gives you the call), and sit there until he taps. The game already knows how to dim everything and wait - the battle does it every turn (F-044). Point that same trick at the moments worth remembering. Small, and it makes Art feel lucky instead of pecked.

title: Junior buttons that show what they are about to do
kevin: Art's CRY, SHINY and RNDM buttons become pictures of their own answers.
acceptance: scenes: in junior mode the CRY, SHINY and RNDM tiles render content derived from the current species rather than a fixed category icon
notes: Two of Art's six buttons are arrows and need nothing - an arrow is a direction he already owns. The other three are a speaker, sparkles and a dice with a word underneath, and all three are abstractions that only resolve once you read the word. A dice means 'random' to someone who has played board games with a grown-up who explained probability; to Art it is a dice. Draw SHINY as this very Pokemon in its shiny colours, CRY as this Pokemon's head with sound rings, RNDM as a blurred unknown silhouette. Same six buttons, same layout, same code path - the glyphs just become specific to the thing on screen. Costs Gabe nothing; he keeps his labels. Pairs naturally with B-010, which is the same principle one row up.
